newsitem.title: UK: British ads showing Blair with demon eyes banned.
newsitem.headline: British ads showing Blair with demon eyes banned.

text.p: Britain's main advertising watchdog banned on Wednesday a Conservative Party campaign advertisement that showed opposition Labour leader Tony Blair with demonic eyes.
The ads, appearing with the slogan "New Labour, New Danger", were run in some British newspapers this month and had been planned to go on billboards across the country.

The Advertising Standards Authority (ASA) ruled that they broke an industry code banning advertisers from portraying politicians and other public figures in an offensive or adverse way without prior permission.
Opposition politicians, church leaders and newspaper leader writers had joined an outcry against the advertisements, saying they represented unacceptably nasty political campaigning.
They were created for the ruling Conservative Party by M&C Saatchi, the agency set up last year by Maurice Saatchi and his brother, Charles.
In December 1994 Maurice was kicked out of Saatchi & Saatchi Advertising, the agency which he and his brother created in 1970 and which previously handled much Conservative publicity.
The Advertising Standards Authority has no statutory power to enforce its ban, since Britain's advertising industry is self-regulatory.
But, in practice, advertisers, media owners and ad agencies rarely disobey it, since they want to avoid the negative publicity.
